title: Scientific Observation
summary: Science starts with careful measurement. A measurement has a value, a unit and an uncertainty.

title: Density
summary: Density (mass per unit volume) is a property of a material that does not depend on the size of the sample.

title: Identifying Materials
summary: Comparing measured properties with reference data lets you identify substances — and shows why one property is rarely enough.

title: Spectroscopy
summary: Every element emits light at its own characteristic wavelengths, a fingerprint used from forensics to astronomy.

title: Minerals and Rocks
summary: Minerals are naturally occurring crystalline compounds; rocks are mixtures of minerals.

title: Conductors and Insulators
summary: Metals conduct electricity because some of their electrons are free to move; insulators hold their electrons tightly.

title: Electric Circuits
summary: Current flows only around a complete loop; a battery provides the potential difference that drives it.

title: Ohm's Law
summary: For many conductors the current is proportional to the voltage: V = IR.

title: Series and Parallel
summary: Resistances add in series; in parallel each branch gets the full voltage and the currents add.

title: Energy Conversion
summary: Generators, motors, lamps and solar cells convert energy from one form to another — never with 100 % efficiency.

title: Electrochemistry
summary: Electric current can drive chemical reactions; the amount of product is fixed by the charge passed (Faraday's law).

title: Chemical Reactions
summary: In a chemical reaction atoms are rearranged into new substances. Balanced equations show the same atoms on both sides.

title: Conservation of Mass
summary: In a closed system the total mass never changes during a reaction.

title: Acids and Bases
summary: Acids donate hydrogen ions and bases accept them; pH is a logarithmic scale of hydrogen-ion concentration.

title: Gas Laws
summary: For an ideal gas PV = nRT: pressure, volume and temperature are linked.

title: Temperature
summary: Temperature measures the average kinetic energy of particles; absolute temperature is measured in kelvin.

title: Phase Changes
summary: During melting and boiling, added energy changes the state of a substance instead of its temperature.

title: Separating Mixtures
summary: Mixtures can be separated by physical processes — filtration, evaporation, distillation — because their components keep their own properties.

title: Thermal Insulation
summary: Insulators slow down heat transfer by conduction, convection and radiation.

title: Graphs and Models
summary: A graph reveals relationships in data; the slope and intercept of a best-fit line are measurable quantities.

title: Reflection and Refraction
summary: Light reflects at equal angles and bends (refracts) when it passes between materials with different refractive indices.

title: Lenses and Images
summary: A converging lens forms images whose positions follow the thin lens equation.

title: Microscopy
summary: Microscopes reveal cells and crystal structures far too small to see with the naked eye.

title: Motion
summary: Velocity is the rate of change of position; acceleration is the rate of change of velocity.

title: Mechanical Energy
summary: Energy is conserved: potential energy becomes kinetic energy, and friction turns some into heat.

title: Simple Machines
summary: Machines can reduce the force needed, but they cannot reduce the energy needed; efficiency is always below 100 %.
